_comment: Phase D regime (b): SPARSE model x prompt interaction (study plan 8.5(b)).
PROVISIONAL -- nothing here is frozen until E3.
RESCOPED. The original regime (b) was to build a saturated interaction
model with a shrinkage prior and ask whether the interaction exists. That
question is already answered: with 6 models x 3 prompts the interaction
columns and the residual cell space are the SAME 10 dimensions (verified
by rank), so 'is there an interaction?' IS 'is sigma_cell > 0?', which
h_m01_size already estimates. A saturated model would be a
reparameterization, not new information, so none is built here.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is the SHAPE. A Gaussian sigma_cell assumes the 10
interaction dimensions are exchangeable. RQ3's substantive claim -- some
models react to a prompt and others do not -- is a SPARSITY claim, and an
exchangeable prior smears a lone deviation across all the cells. So:
simulate a spike on ONE cell, fit the EXISTING h_m01_size, and ask whether
that cell is localized. Only a failure justifies building a horseshoe
variant, and then the build cost is warranted rather than speculative.
TWO ARMS PER ITERATION, and the control is what makes it readable:
sparse -- one cell shifted by spike_magnitude, all others exactly 0
dense  -- a Gaussian interaction of the SAME interaction-subspace norm
Both are supplied as data (cell_offset) with sigma_cell_sd = 0, under the
same sim seed, so gamma, beta, delta and the copy pattern are shared and
the arms differ ONLY in shape. Without the dense arm, 'the spiked cell was
flagged' could not be separated from 'some cell is always flagged when the
cell-level SD is large' -- the same confound the MAR arm removes in (c).
factors [6,3] gives J=18 and P=7, the real design structure. J=18 is NOT
optional here: the interaction question does not exist at J=6, P=2.
COST. Two fits per iteration at J=18. The only J=18 measurement in hand is
menus/cell 60 (22,703 s/iter, ONE fit), and that number itself came in at
1.75x a linear-in-M_total extrapolation. So the per-iteration cost here is
UNMEASURED. Run --measure first and size n_iterations from the result; do
not trust the number below as a prediction.
spike_magnitude 1.0 is a log-alpha shift, i.e. alpha up by a factor 2.7 in
the affected cell -- far outside the 8.3 ROPE of log 1.25. Deliberately
large for a first pass: if the Gaussian model cannot localize an effect
this big, it cannot localize anything, and the question is settled cheaply.
MEASURED on this design: a centered single-cell spike keeps 0.588 of its
squared norm in the 10-dim interaction subspace, so main_effect_leak is
0.642 of the norm and the true residual SD across cells is 0.176 -- close
to the 0.239 prior mean of sigma_cell, i.e. a plausible magnitude, not a
cartoon one. Verified: rank([1 X]) = 8, residual dims = 10, matching the
aliasing result exactly.
menus/cell 30 and rho_copy 0.9 match the regime (a) and (c) reference
cells so the timing basis is comparable within J.
